FIXUP: FROMLIST: remoteproc: mt8183: add reserved memory manager API 0day reports: drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp.c:374:2: note: in expansion of macro 'dev_info' drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp.c:375:4: warning: format '%llx' expects argument of type 'long long unsigned int', but argument 3 has type 'phys_addr_t {aka unsigned int}' [-Wformat=] drivers/remoteproc/mtk_scp.c:403:4: warning: format '%llx' expects argument of type 'long long unsigned int', but argument 3 has type 'unsigned int' [-Wformat=] The actual parameters are of type phys_addr_t, so we should really use %pa to display it. However, %pa expects a _pointer_ to the address, not the address itself, as parameter. Since the displayed value is often the result of a calculation, and not just an address, we can not consistently use %pa. Use typecasts to unsigned long long instead. CRAS: iodev - Protect ext_module by pipline lock When web app enables APM in CRAS, the active playback or echo reference iodev will have APM run as one of the modules in its dsp pipeline. There's a special case when using BT headset that when it gets disconnected, the silent playback device is activated and configured to run APM in audio thread because the BT iodev cannot do I/O anymore Later when main thread handles the event from bluetoothd to remove BT iodev, the silent playback device gets configured to run APM again. And that could cause crash because the cras_apm_reverse_module is being accessed by two threads. To fix that, move ext_dsp_module->configure call to between the get/put call of dsp pipeline so the mutex protects it from being accessed by two threads at the same time. BUG=chromium:970165 TEST=Apply full patch series, launch appr.tc and connect LG HBS700 headset. In bluetooth settings UI, repeatedly connect/disconnect headset 20-30 times to verify CRAS doesn't crash. Change-Id: Ia10d9135ee775e2d14017a09bfc0f429ab4dc364 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1647213 Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

CRAS: dsp - NULL ext_dsp_module should set into pipeline When web app uses CRAS APM and the playback iodev switches, the cras_apm_reverse_module would detach and attach to different dsp pipelines of the iodev used as echo reference. There is a bug that when swtich playback away from iodev X, the sink module of dsp pipeline still points to the APM module for a short while before it closes. At this moment, main thread configures iodev Y by attaching the same APM module to its dsp pipeline, and that could cause crash. To fix this problem, modify the API to set NULL ext_dsp_module into the DSP pipeline/module layer, to ensure that it doesn't leak or be used in two thread simultaneously. BUG=chromium:970165 TEST=Apply full patch series, launch appr.tc and use LG HBS700 headset. In bluetooth settings UI, repeatedly connect/disconnect headset for 20 times to verify CRAS doesn't crash. Change-Id: Ifbf688d3e22ef13a303fb30915f6a932528a7d07 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1647214 Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

CRAS: apm_list - Make echo ref tracking more reliable Below changes are made to ensure the echo ref tracking is reliable in apm_list regardless of how the device enable/disable events come from cras_iodev_list. - If APM rmod already tracking the same iodev as echo ref, don't bother configure it again. - If APM rmod was tracking another iodev, configure its dsp pipeline so it no longer points back to APM rmod. BUG=chromium:970165 TEST=Use appr.tc with BT headset.
